who.text: Mu is an older woman who knows Zei through

start.text: Before Zei's quarter-final, she warns him that on a team, diplomacy matters: "You're a math guy, not a diplomat."
. From the sidelines she sees that Zei and his rival Bai don't get along, and that their side is suffering for it
. Afterwards she tells them the secret: she had pushed the priests to be more creative, and the teams were not chosen at random. The game was "a psychological trial", and they passed
. After the next match she draws the lesson: "it's not just thinking well that matters, it's also hiding your thoughts"
. Then, with Den, she tells Zei what Minpentai is really for: "It's military training."

who.text: Lord Ephelion is the
's consul, also called its ambassador, to
. He is the Arctics' voice in Veridia: his messages turn up on posters and on screens

start.text: His open letter tells Veridia's young people that their country is too comfortable, and asks them to build a stronger one with the Arctics: "Join us, and we will build it together."
. He debates Professor Sylka live, arguing that economic growth is the only lasting progress
. Gladias, listening on the
, calls him "A gifted demagogue"
, and others complain about "Lord Ephelion giving his sermons all the time."

later.text: His broadcast cuts into a sports game in a restaurant, telling people that "Life is not fair - and should not be fair." Seila gets up to unplug the screen
. When the Arctics invade the province of Northshore, he is reported to be there
. Gladias and Seila's daughter Lily turns out to have been following his sermons, and runs away from home
. Seila sums him up: "Ephelion and Delwart are not intellectuals, they are propagandists."
In her reading, his goal is "to inspire people inside Veridia to join the Arctic cause."

drives.text: In his own words: strength, winning and growth. "Build the future."
